item: U-01 NMPA dedicated New Approach Methodology (NAM) programme or non-animal-methods policy instrument
queries_tried: WebSearch 'NMPA breakthrough therapy designation number granted 2025 China priority review MFDS GIFT global innovative products fast track Korea number designated' | WebSearch 'NMPA 2025 innovative drug approvals number 40 class 1 China CDE review timeline priority review 2026' | WebFetch english.nmpa.gov.cn/2025-10/14/c_1138494.htm | WebSearch 'European Commission roadmap phase out animal testing 2026 EMA 3Rs working party NAM EU pharmaceutical legislation revision non-animal methods' (used to check whether CN appears in comparative NAM coverage)
failure_reason: No NMPA or CDE instrument dedicated to New Approach Methodologies was returned by any query. English-language NMPA portal coverage is limited to approval-process announcements; the Chinese-language CDE technical guideline index was not reachable through the available search index in this environment.
alt_sources_tried: (1) english.nmpa.gov.cn direct fetch - returned only the clinical trial review announcement, no NAM content; (2) Nature Reviews Drug Discovery 'Approvals by the China NMPA in 2025' - redirected to an authentication endpoint (HTTP 303) and could not be read; (3) DIA Global Forum '2025 NMPA Approvals' article - covers approval counts only, no NAM policy; (4) IntuitionLabs China NMPA regulatory guide - secondary aggregator, no NAM instrument named
best_estimate: China most likely operates NAM acceptance through ICH implementation (S1B(R1) weight-of-evidence and M15 MIDD, both of which China is bound to as an ICH regulatory member) rather than through a standalone national NAM programme comparable to FDA ISTAND or the EC roadmap.
best_estimate_basis: China joined ICH in 2017 and NMPA has systematically transposed ICH guidelines; ICH S1B(R1) was adopted in 2022 and ICH M15 reached Step 4 on 29 Jan 2026 with implementation obligations falling on all ICH regulatory members [E-4010][E-4011]. Absent any located national instrument, ICH transposition is the parsimonious explanation. Confidence in this estimate is deliberately low and it is not used to support any conclusion in the report.

item: U-02 NMPA / CDE published position on acceptance of AI-derived or AI-generated evidence in regulatory submissions
queries_tried: WebSearch 'FDA CDER statement AI-designed molecules generative AI drug candidates regulatory acceptance 2026 no special pathway' | WebSearch 'EMA reflection paper artificial intelligence medicinal product lifecycle 2024 AI workplan 2028 HMA' | WebSearch 'NMPA 2025 innovative drug approvals number 40 class 1 China CDE review timeline priority review 2026' | WebFetch english.nmpa.gov.cn/2025-10/14/c_1138494.htm
failure_reason: No English-language NMPA or CDE guidance, technical guideline or reflection paper on AI in drug development was surfaced by any query. Results for AI-and-regulator queries were dominated by FDA and EMA material.
alt_sources_tried: (1) english.nmpa.gov.cn - no AI content in the reachable announcement set; (2) Nature Reviews Drug Discovery China 2025 approvals article - authentication redirect, unreadable; (3) IntuitionLabs 'China NMPA Drug Approval Pathways: Regulatory Guide' (Apr 2026) - covers pathways and timelines, no AI evidence policy; (4) DIA Global Forum March 2026 NMPA approvals article - approval statistics only
best_estimate: NMPA most likely has no binding AI-evidence acceptance instrument as of Aug 2026, and would assess AI-generated evidence case by case under existing technical review guidelines, consistent with FDA and EMA both still being at draft-guidance and reflection-paper level respectively.
best_estimate_basis: FDA's framework was still draft 19 months after publication [E-4013] and EMA's is a non-binding reflection paper [E-4016]; no ICH AI guideline exists. It would be surprising for NMPA to be ahead of both. Not used to support any conclusion in the report.

item: U-03 Exact cumulative CBER RMAT designation totals: requests received, granted, denied, withdrawn, as of the most recent FDA data cutoff
queries_tried: WebSearch 'CBER RMAT designation cumulative number granted 2025 2026 breakthrough therapy designation counts CDER total requests granted' | WebFetch fda.gov/vaccines-blood-biologics/.../cumulative-cber-regenerative-medicine-advanced-therapy-rmat-designation-requests-received-fiscal | WebFetch cacmap.fda.gov mirror of the same path | WebSearch 'CBER 2025 biological approvals number gene therapy 2026 Office of Therapeutic Products staffing reorganization review backlog'
failure_reason: www.fda.gov returned HTTP 401 to the fetch tool for every path attempted in this environment, and the cacmap.fda.gov mirror returned HTTP 403. The search-summary layer returned internally inconsistent fiscal-year figures (a 'FY2025: 91 requests, 50 granted' reading that is inconsistent with the cumulative-by-fiscal-year structure of the FDA table), so no numeric value could be asserted without risking a fabricated figure.
alt_sources_tried: (1) www.fda.gov cumulative RMAT table - HTTP 401; (2) cacmap.fda.gov mirror - HTTP 403; (3) AABB news item 'CBER Releases Updated RMAT Designation Requests, Approvals and Withdrawals' (21 Jul 2025) - located but the numeric content was not exposed in the search summary; (4) Pharmaceutical Technology 'How FDA's New RMAT Guidance Impacts Clinical, CMC Strategies' - narrative only; (5) FDA Expedited Programs for Regenerative Medicine Therapies guidance PDF (fda.gov/media/120267) - policy text, no counts
best_estimate: Cumulative RMAT requests received since 13 Dec 2016 are most likely in the range 350-450 with roughly 130-190 granted, i.e. a grant rate in the 35-45% band.
best_estimate_basis: The FDA table is cumulative-by-fiscal-year and the two readings recovered (FY2024 ~59 and FY2025 ~91 on one axis, with 43 and 50 granted) are consistent with an annual request flow in the 40-90 range across nine fiscal years and a grant rate below half, which the search layer stated explicitly. The report therefore asserts only the qualitative facts (programme start date, publication of granted/withdrawn/approved lists, grant rate under half) in E-4036 and asserts no numeric total. This estimate is not used in any calculation.

item: U-04 NMPA/CDE and MFDS reviewer headcounts, for like-for-like comparison with CDER+CBER 6,383, EMA ~897 and PMDA ~873
queries_tried: WebSearch 'EMA 2025 annual report number of staff CHMP positive opinions new active substances 2025 PMDA number of reviewers staff 2025' | WebSearch 'EMA number of staff 2025 annual report establishment plan employees budget scientific committees workload applications received' | WebSearch 'NMPA 2025 innovative drug approvals number 40 class 1 China CDE review timeline priority review 2026' | WebSearch 'NMPA breakthrough therapy designation number granted 2025 China priority review MFDS GIFT global innovative products fast track Korea number designated'
failure_reason: Neither CDE nor MFDS publishes a reviewer headcount in any English-language source returned. EMA and PMDA figures were recoverable; CN and KR were not.
alt_sources_tried: (1) english.nmpa.gov.cn - organisational pages not surfaced by the search index; (2) mfds.go.kr English GIFT page (fetched successfully) - describes the programme and its statistics but contains no staffing data; (3) EMA annual activity report 2025 PDF - EMA only; (4) Wikipedia PMDA/EMA entries - JP and EU only; (5) DIA Global Forum March 2026 NMPA article - approvals only
best_estimate: CDE headcount is most plausibly in the 1,000-1,600 range and MFDS drug-review staff in the low hundreds.
best_estimate_basis: CDE processed 289 approved new drug applications in 2025 [E-4042]; PMDA achieves ~873 staff with ~560 technical reviewers against a much smaller approval volume [E-4027], so a CDE figure below PMDA's would be implausible given China's throughput, while a figure approaching CDER's 5,044 would almost certainly have been reported. This estimate appears only as a gap marker in the region table and supports no conclusion.

item: U-05 PMDA and MFDS novel-approval counts for CY2025 on a basis comparable to FDA novel approvals (46) and EMA new active substances (38)
queries_tried: WebSearch 'EMA 2025 annual report number of staff CHMP positive opinions new active substances 2025 PMDA number of reviewers staff 2025' | WebSearch 'PMDA Sakigake designation number granted products approved Japan conditional time-limited approval regenerative medicine number of products 2025' | WebSearch 'NMPA breakthrough therapy designation number granted 2025 China priority review MFDS GIFT global innovative products fast track Korea number designated' | WebFetch mfds.go.kr/eng/wpge/m_1176/de011009l001.do
failure_reason: PMDA's English annual review-report pages were not surfaced with a CY2025 novel-approval count, and MFDS's English pages carry GIFT designation statistics only (56 designated, 34 approved as of 8 Feb 2024) rather than an annual new-active-substance count.
alt_sources_tried: (1) pmda.go.jp/english/review-services/reviews/0001.html - listed in results but no count exposed; (2) pmda.go.jp List of Approved Regenerative Medical Products Apr 2015 - Nov 2025 PDF - regenerative products only, not all novel approvals; (3) mfds.go.kr English GIFT page - fetched, no annual novel count; (4) Korea Biomedical Review article on 2024 innovative medical device designations - devices, not drugs; (5) PMDA Updates 2025 Autumn PDF - newsletter, no count
best_estimate: PMDA most likely approved roughly 35-50 new active ingredients in FY2025 and MFDS roughly 20-35 new drugs in CY2025.
best_estimate_basis: PMDA's historical run-rate of new active ingredient approvals has sat in the 30-50 band and Japan is the third-largest pharmaceutical market; MFDS's GIFT programme alone accounted for 34 approvals across roughly 17 months to Feb 2024 [E-4041], implying a total national new-drug approval count well above that but below EMA's 38 new active substances. Both figures appear only as gap markers in the region table and support no conclusion.

item: U-06 Count of PDUFA goal dates missed by FDA in CY2026, to test whether the FY2025 workforce reduction produced measurable slippage
queries_tried: WebSearch 'FDA missed PDUFA goal dates 2026 number late decisions review delays tracking analysis' | WebSearch 'FDA PDUFA goal date performance 2025 2026 missed goal dates percentage on-time novel approvals CDER count' | WebSearch 'CDER novel drug approvals 2025 total number 2026 year to date FDA missed PDUFA dates layoffs impact' | WebFetch insights.citeline.com Pink Sheet 'US FDA Feeling Layoff Impact? NDA/BLA First Half Approvals Down' | WebFetch michbio.org 'Reports Document FDA Review Delays'
failure_reason: FDA's own FDA-TRACK dashboard marks FY2025 and FY2026 data preliminary and updates quarterly, and www.fda.gov returned HTTP 401 to the fetch tool so the dashboard could not be read directly. The two trade analyses located either withheld the figures behind a paywall (Citeline) or contained only qualitative statements (MichBio, published Apr 2025 and therefore predating the period of interest).
alt_sources_tried: (1) www.fda.gov FDA-TRACK PDUFA dashboards - HTTP 401; (2) Citeline Pink Sheet H1 2026 approvals article - fetched, headline confirms direction but the numeric table is not in the retrievable body; (3) MichBio 'Reports Document FDA Review Delays' - fetched, qualitative only, dated 24 Apr 2025; (4) Statista key measures of US CDER drug approvals - 2025 only; (5) BiopharmaWatch and Assyro PDUFA calendars - forward-looking target dates, not realised performance; (6) Osprey Life Sciences 'Measuring the Impact of FDA Personnel Cuts in 2025' - located but not a goal-date count
best_estimate: CY2026 on-time PDUFA performance is most likely in the 88-95% band, i.e. somewhat below the 96% recorded for 2025 but not a collapse.
best_estimate_basis: The direction is supported by two independent signals: NDA/BLA approvals fell in H1 2026 relative to prior first halves [E-4028], and individual three-month extensions are documented (for example LEQEMBI IQLIK extended to 24 Aug 2026). Against that, CDER novel approvals recovered in H1 2026 and the CNPV pilot delivered actions in 24-79 days during the same period [E-4033], which is inconsistent with systemic slippage. The report treats CY2026 slippage as an open tail risk and draws no conclusion from this estimate.
